title: Linear structure of the rationalization
statement:
In the situation of [def-sfb-rationalization-quotient], for every $m\in M$ and every
object $Y$ of $\mathcal T[M^{-1}]$, the morphism $m\cdot\mathrm{id}_Y$ is an isomorphism.
Consequently, for every localization $A$ of $R$ at $M$ (for instance $A=R[M^{-1}]$), the
action of $R$ on $\mathcal T[M^{-1}]$ extends uniquely to an $A$-linear structure, with
$\bar r\cdot f=r\cdot f$ for the image $\bar r\in A$ of $r\in R$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal D=\mathcal T[M^{-1}]$ and let $Q:\mathcal T\to\mathcal D$ be the triangulated localization of [def-sfb-rationalization-quotient]. By the definitions of [def-weil-triangulated-category], a triangulated category is additive, hence preadditive, and a triangulated (exact) functor is an additive functor. Apply [lem-sfb-additive-localization-linear] to $Q$ and $W_M$: equip $\mathcal D$ with its induced $R$-linear structure, so $Q(rf)=rQ(f)$. The same node says that $Q$ inverts $W_M$ and that every $Y\in\mathcal D$ has an isomorphism $e:Q(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$.

source.place: First sentence and the R-linearity implicit in the second sentence.

proof.text: Fix $m\in M$ and $Y\in\mathcal D$. Choose $e:Q(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ as above. By [lem-sfb-smul-id-in-w], $m\cdot\mathrm{id}_X\in W_M$, so [lem-sfb-additive-localization-linear] makes $Q(m\cdot\mathrm{id}_X)=m\cdot\mathrm{id}_{Q(X)}$ invertible. Bilinearity gives $e\circ(m\cdot\mathrm{id}_{Q(X)})\circ e^{-1}=m\cdot(e\circ e^{-1})=m\cdot\mathrm{id}_Y$. Its inverse is $e\circ(m\cdot\mathrm{id}_{Q(X)})^{-1}\circ e^{-1}$, as direct multiplication of the two composites shows. This proves the first clause for every object, rather than only for objects written literally as $Q(X)$.

source.place: First three sentences: invert the scalar map and transfer along an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-category-center-linear] to form the commutative ring $Z(\mathcal D)$ of natural endomorphisms of the identity and the scalar ring map $\rho:R\to Z(\mathcal D)$, $\rho(r)_Y=r\cdot\mathrm{id}_Y$. Every $\rho(m)$, $m\in M$, is a unit: set $u_Y=(m\cdot\mathrm{id}_Y)^{-1}$. For $f:X\to Y$, naturality of $\rho(m)$ says $\rho(m)_Y\circ f=f\circ\rho(m)_X$; multiplying on the left by $u_Y$ and on the right by $u_X$ gives $f\circ u_X=u_Y\circ f$. Thus $u=(u_Y)$ belongs to $Z(\mathcal D)$, and its two products with $\rho(m)$ are the identity componentwise. This explicitly supplies the units required for ring localization.

source.place: Fourth sentence: the ring map to the center sends M to units.

proof.text: Let $i:R\to A$ be any localization at $M$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] to $\rho:R\to Z(\mathcal D)$, which sends $M$ to units by step 3. This gives a unique ring map $\phi:A\to Z(\mathcal D)$ with $\phi(i(r))=\rho(r)$, and $\phi(i(r)i(m)^{-1})=\rho(r)\rho(m)^{-1}$. The cited node uses the fraction model $M^{-1}R$; for any other localization model $A$, the universal maps between $A$ and $M^{-1}R$ are inverse because each composite extends the original map from $R$, and uniqueness makes each composite the identity. Compose the displayed map with this canonical identification. No assumption that $R\to A$ is injective is used.

source.place: Tag 00CP, proposition-universal-property-localization, existence and uniqueness; applied as in the fifth sentence of the blueprint proof.

proof.text: Apply the reverse construction of [lem-sfb-category-center-linear] to $\phi$: on each morphism group set $a\cdot f=f\circ\phi(a)_X$ for $f:X\to Y$. The cited node supplies the module laws and bilinearity of composition, hence this is an $A$-linear structure. For $r\in R$, the formula in step 4 gives $i(r)\cdot f=f\circ\rho(r)_X=f\circ(r\cdot\mathrm{id}_X)=r\cdot f$, using the original $R$-bilinearity in the last equality. This is the asserted compatibility with the $R$-action.

source.place: Last sentence and the compatibility formula in the item statement.

proof.text: For uniqueness, let $\star$ be another $A$-linear structure on the same preadditive category extending the given $R$-action. By [lem-sfb-category-center-linear], $\psi(a)_X=a\star\mathrm{id}_X$ defines a ring map $\psi:A\to Z(\mathcal D)$, and compatibility gives $\psi(i(r))=\rho(r)$. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] implies $\psi=\phi$. Finally $a\star f=f\circ(a\star\mathrm{id}_X)=f\circ\psi(a)_X=f\circ\phi(a)_X=a\cdot f$, where the first equality is bilinearity and the identity law. Thus the scalar operations, and hence the linear structures on the fixed morphism groups, coincide.

source.place: The uniqueness in the fifth sentence and the equivalence claimed in the last sentence, with the recovery of scalar action written out.
